TYPE CHECK: The candidate value "cell line" is a valid category for the material_type field.
SOURCE CHECK: The paper explicitly mentions the use of HEK 293 and HeLa cells, which are standard cell lines.
TRUTH CHECK: The use of these cell lines for protein expression and interactome analysis is factually correct.
COMPLETENESS CHECK: The full set of extracted values is incomplete because the proteomics analysis (interactome) was performed using HEK 293 cells, but the study also extensively used mouse tissues (inner ear and brain) for other analyses. However, for the specific MS experiment described in the "Identification of WT and mutant OSBPL2 interactors" section, only cell lines were used. Wait, looking at the "material_type" definition, it must match what was actually used in the experiment. The MS experiment used HEK 293 cells. But the paper also mentions "inner ear tissues" and "brain tissues" in the context of other experiments. Usually, material_type refers to the sample source for the MS analysis. In this paper, the LC-MS/MS was performed on proteins extracted from HEK 293 cells. Therefore, "cell line" is correct for the MS part. However, the study as a whole uses both. If the pipeline is extracting material types for the MS experiment specifically, "cell line" is exhaustive. If it is for the whole paper, it is missing "tissue". Given the context of proteomics metadata, it usually refers to the MS sample.
